subject: social
title: Makers and Buyers
about: Producers make or grow things and consumers buy and use them, how bread, milk, eggs, wool and wood get from the farm or factory to the store, and trading. NC 1.E.1.4: why people trade goods and services.
tip: At the store, pick up one food and ask him who made or grew it and how it got here.

cards.q: A person who makes or grows things to sell is called a...
cards.note: Farmers, bakers and builders are producers.

cards.q: A person who buys and uses things is called a...
cards.note: When you eat the bread you bought, you are a consumer.

cards.q: A baker makes bread to sell. Is the baker a producer or a consumer?
cards.note: The baker made the bread, so the baker is the producer.

cards.q: You buy a snack and eat it. Are you a producer or a consumer?
cards.note: You bought it and used it, so you are the consumer.

cards.q: Mr. Lee sells corn at his farm stand. Then he buys shoes at a store. When he buys shoes, what is he?
cards.note: People can be producers and consumers at different times.

cards.q: A farm where rows of apple trees grow is called an...
cards.note: Many North Carolina orchards are in the mountains.

cards.q: Bread is made from flour. Flour is made from a plant. Which plant?
cards.note: Farmers grow wheat, a mill grinds it into flour, and a baker bakes the bread.

cards.q: The milk at the store comes from which farm animal?
cards.note: Dairy farmers milk cows, and a truck takes the milk to be bottled.

cards.q: The eggs at the store come from which farm animal?
cards.note: A hen is a grown-up female chicken.

cards.q: Warm sweaters are often made from wool. Which animal gives us wool?
cards.note: Wool is cut off the sheep, spun into yarn and knit into clothes.

cards.q: Many houses are built with wood. Where does wood come from?
cards.note: Loggers cut the trees, a sawmill cuts boards, and builders build the house.

cards.q: Carrots grow on a farm. A truck carries them away. Where do they go so people can buy them?
cards.note: Farm, truck, store, then your kitchen.

cards.q: Who moves goods from the farm or factory to the store?
cards.note: Trucks, trains and ships carry goods from place to place.

cards.q: A big building where workers make lots of the same thing, like shoes, is a...
cards.note: Factories use machines to make many things fast.

cards.q: Where do farmers sell fruits and vegetables straight to the people who eat them?
cards.note: At a farmers market, the producer and the consumer meet face to face.

cards.q: Ava gives Ben a sticker. Ben gives Ava a marble. What did Ava and Ben do?
cards.note: A trade can happen with things instead of money.

cards.q: A farmer has lots of eggs and needs bread. A baker has bread and needs eggs. What can they do?
cards.note: Trading helps both people get what they need.

cards.q: When you pay money for a toy, what are you trading for the toy?
cards.note: Buying is a trade: money for a good or a service.
